title: What If the Sahara Desert Turned Green?

scenes.text: What if the Sahara turned green? It already has. Hippos swam there.
About eleven thousand years ago it was dotted with lakes, rivers, grasslands and even forests.
The cause was a slow wobble in Earth's orbit that strengthened the West African monsoon.
That wobble repeats about every twenty-one thousand years, so the Sahara has flipped between green and desert before.
Ice ages blocked it. Huge ice sheets cooled the air and weakened the monsoon, so the desert stayed dry.
It dried out fast, within a few thousand years, and scientists still debate whether people sped it up.

description:
What if the Sahara turned green?
It already did, more than once. Lakes, rivers, grasslands and hippos covered it about 11,000 years ago, driven by wobbles in Earth's orbit that repeat roughly every 21,000 years.
